sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only, p. 94 (PDF p. 102): 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern.. it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable.' Maiwa is listed as dialect (a) of Masenrempulu (Kec. Maiwa, Kab. Enrekang, and Kab. Sidenrang) but the only Masenrempulu wordlist (MSR) was taken at Enrekang; no Maiwa data.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Google Books snippet proves it contains a 'tekanan kata' section stating that Massenrempulu word stress is phonemic (contrastive), with examples (a-lai.., tunu-i, pollo); it explicitly compares the Duri, Endekan and Maiwa dialects, so it is the closest thing to a Maiwa stress statement in print. Needed to see the rule, the examples and which dialect(s) show the contrast.
